Amazing to think the Sun gets through 600million tons of hydrogen per second yet still has enough for another 4 billion years or so.

Scientists have captured the highest-resolution images of the sun ever made, revealing astonishing new details. These incredible photos were taken using the four-meter NSF Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii, the world's most powerful solar telescope. The images show a magnetically turbulent area on the edge of a cool sunspot, in the visible outer layer of our home star. Combined with cutting-edge simulations, researchers say their new photos reveal something that has never been seen before.

Owner Megan Share, 28, says Milo uses the feel of the ground beneath his hooves to build a picture of the world around him.
